item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.32), AMZN Bullish (+0.25)] The Biggest Catalyst for Alphabet Stock May Not Be Search
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.32), AMZN Bullish (+0.25)
Alphabet's stock performance is increasingly driven by its Google Cloud segment rather than its traditional Search business. Google Cloud saw an 82% revenue growth and holds a $514 billion backlog, surpassing Alphabet's entire 2025 revenue, yet the stock trades at a significantly lower P/E ratio compared to competitors like Microsoft and Amazon. Analysts project a 50% upside for Alphabet, with a price target of $504.76, primarily fueled by the accelerating Cloud growth and its undervalued position in the market.

item.title: [MSFT Bearish (-0.34)] Judge orders Microsoft to spill internal docs and scour execs' comms in secondhand licensing case
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bearish (-0.34)

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.22)] How power is becoming the new geography of growth
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.22)

This shift highlights a significant mismatch between the rapid development of digital infrastructure and the much slower expansion of power capacity, leading to potential constraints on future growth. As power moves from a mere utility cost to a strategic growth determinant, the physical availability of electricity will increasingly shape the economic landscape.

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.45)] Jensen Huang Says Hyperscalers Get This ‘Almost Always Wrong’ — Nvidia Has a Workaround
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Bullish (+0.45)
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang believes hyperscalers are "almost always wrong" in their capacity planning due to the rapidly changing AI market and their annual planning cycles. To address this, Nvidia is focusing on building a vast network of nimble regional cloud providers, which can react faster to local demand and infrastructure needs. This strategy helps Nvidia ensure its hardware is widely consumed and reinforces a shift in AI infrastructure where electricity, land, and data center capacity are as crucial as the chips themselves.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.25)] OpenAI, Microsoft fend off part of software developer lawsuit over AI training
item.description:

The developers alleged that the companies misused code from GitHub to train generative AI systems, specifically violating the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA). The court upheld a previous ruling that OpenAI and Microsoft were not liable under the DMCA, differentiating these claims from traditional copyright infringement.

The issue affects various Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server versions, with Microsoft indicating it is working on further solutions.

item.title: [MSFT Bearish (-0.31)] Microsoft Warns Passkey Phishing Attacks Are Leading to Cloud Account Takeovers
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bearish (-0.31)
Microsoft has issued a warning about an active social engineering campaign where attackers impersonate IT help desks to trick employees with fake passkey setup requests. These phishing attacks aim to compromise employee identities and gain unauthorized access to corporate cloud data, allowing attackers to establish persistence and exfiltrate sensitive information from services like SharePoint, OneDrive, and Exchange. The company advises organizations to enforce phishing-resistant MFA and block unnecessary authentication flows to mitigate these threats.

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.04)] Microsoft Asks Government Agencies to Commit Now, Deliver Features Later

This strategy presents a commercial risk due to annual federal procurement cycles and the need for agencies to budget for a suite that isn't fully available yet. Investors are closely watching conversion rates from earlier no-cost Copilot deployments and awaiting disclosures on per-seat pricing and workload authorizations to gauge the potential government revenue impact.

item.title: [TSM Neutral (+0.02)] Why Taiwan’s Silicon Shield Is Failing
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Neutral (+0.02)
Taiwan's "silicon shield," stemming from its dominance in advanced semiconductor manufacturing, is facing challenges as China invests heavily in chip self-reliance, particularly in mature-node chips. While Taiwan still holds leverage in cutting-edge chips, China's increasing capacity in 28-nanometer chips threatens to make Taiwan's shield irrelevant for its own economy, potentially leading to a more fragile global trade environment with rising chip prices. This shift means that the geopolitical importance of Taiwan's chip production will no longer solely rely on the most advanced technologies, but also on the control of common chip manufacturing.
